A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core framework, and experiments. The main text, equations, figures, and both appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Tiny ImageNet continual-learning, CIFAR-10 cloning, and bit-flipping experiments, including accuracy, loss, effective rank, and unit-level statistics.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds numerical activation analyses in Figures A.1–A.3 and additional recovery trajectories in Figure B.1.

M1.justification: The cloning procedure, architectures, normalization interventions, noisy SGD, dropout, and continual backpropagation procedures are retained. Revised mathematical characterizations do not establish changes to their implementation.

E1.justification: Tiny ImageNet continual learning, CIFAR-10 cloning, and bit-flipping remain unchanged in coverage. v2 additionally reports synthetic Gaussian activation evaluations and generated correlation-matrix probes in Appendices A.1–A.2, extending the documented evaluation scenarios beyond the learning benchmarks.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same SGD, Adam, noisy-SGD, dropout, normalization, and continual-backpropagation comparisons. The additional switch schedules retain the SGD-to-CBP comparison; theoretical bound curves do not introduce competing algorithms.

E3.justification: Figure B.1 adds switches after 25% and 75% of five million samples, retaining the original 50% switch. New analyses interpolate correlation matrices from identity to a dense random matrix and evaluate activation freezing using |f'| < 0.01. Existing benchmark training settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures A.1–A.3 add direct numerical checks of the decorrelation-gap and rank-gain bounds and systematic activation-modulation analyses of freezing across six activation functions. Figure B.1 also adds sensitivity to recovery-intervention timing. These substantially expand empirical examination of the proposed mechanisms.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose five experimental seeds and describe figure uncertainty as standard deviations in Appendix B.1.3. The additional trajectories retain this reporting practice; no changed run counts or statistical estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: v2 adds a substantive set of numerical findings: Figure A.1 reports rank gains above the derived bounds for ReLU, GELU, SiLU, and tanh; Figures A.2–A.3 quantify activation-dependent freezing tradeoffs; Figure B.1 adds early- and late-switch loss/rank trajectories. Existing benchmark plots and the original midpoint-switch results are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.1 replace the monotonicity-focused treatment with a universal quartic-gap bound and an explicit rank-gain lower bound using newly defined decorrelation strength and potential. v2 also corrects row/column conditions in the cloning theorem and proof, states additional assumptions explicitly, and distinguishes continuous-flow invariance from discrete updates.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its characterization from stable manifolds to invariant submanifolds and strengthens the intervention claim from exploring potential mitigation to demonstrating restoration. The central frozen/cloned-unit mechanisms, rank-plasticity tension, and conclusion remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.1 characterizes LoP as specific to the rich feature-learning regime, introducing a substantive applicability claim absent from v1. Section 3 removes the information-bottleneck explanation and revises the correlation-based mechanism. Adam's failure to escape changes from an unexplained exception to behavior predicted by the retained invariance argument.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link below the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. The detailed cloning implementation, architecture configurations, hyperparameters, hardware, and computational-cost disclosures in Appendix B are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chizat et al. (2019) and Woodworth et al. (2020) for the lazy/rich-regime connection, removes the information-bottleneck citation and several introductory references, and sharpens its contrast with symptom-based accounts. The main related-work discussion and geometric-singularity positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, including a new contribution list. Section 3's explanatory narrative and Appendix A.1's proof exposition are substantially reorganized, with a separate empirical rank-plasticity subsection. These changes extend beyond insertion of new scientific results.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual manifold illustration in Figure 1.1 and three multipanel theoretical-validation figures, substantially expanding the graphical exposition. Figure B.1 changes from one plot to three adjacent panels, retaining the original plot centrally. Other benchmark figures preserve their displays.

improvement.justification: The quantitative rank bound, numerical validation, cloning-proof corrections, and code-access information improve precision and support for the existing framework. The gain is limited by new inconsistencies: Theorem 3.1 incorrectly states strict gain for vanishing potential and a linear activation, conflicting with Appendix A.1, and Figure B.1's caption still describes only the original midpoint switch.
